newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian forestry sector exports rise in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian forestry sector exports rise in 1996.

text.p: Indonesia's export earnings from the forestry sector rose to $8.3 billion in 1996 from $7.1 billion in 1995, the official Antara news agency reported on Thursday.
"The prospects of timber products will remain bright in 1997," Forestry Minister Djamaluddin Soeryohadikusumo was quoted as telling a news conference on Tuesday.
He said foreign exchange earnings from plywood rose to $4.7 billion last year from $3.9 billion in 1995, while that for pulp and paper increased to $1.5 billion in 1996 from $1.2 billion.

Soeryohadikusumo said export revenue from furniture and related products rose to $541 million last year from $458.7 million in 1995, while that for rattan and its products was up at $471 million from $368.1 million in 1995.
He said export earnings from processed timber, however, fell to $1.07 billion in 1996 from $1.1 billion the previous year.
The minister attributed the overall increase in the forestry sector's export earnings to several factors, including improved plywood prices and higher export volumes of pulp and paper.
He said the expansion of pulp and paper mills along with the construction of new ones would help boost export volume.
